en: The Philippines has 7,641 islands, which is 534 more than the previously recorded count of 7,107 islands.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at exactly 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers from north to south.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a massive surface area of 911 square kilometers.
Taal Volcano is the second most active volcano in the Philippines, with over 30 historical eruptions recorded.
The Cordillera Administrative Region has exactly six provinces, making it the Philippine region with the fewest provinces.
The Philippine eagle is critically endangered, with only about 400 breeding pairs remaining in the wild forests.
The Philippines experiences an average of 20 tropical cyclones yearly, which is more than most neighboring Asian countries.
The Puerto Princesa Underground River stretches for 8.2 kilometers, making it one of the longest navigable subterranean rivers globally.
The Philippine Sea contains the Philippine Trench, which reaches a massive depth of 10,540 meters below sea level.
The Banaue Rice Terraces span 10,360 square kilometers, covering a much larger area than the entire National Capital Region.
Mount Mayon is famous for its perfect cone, having erupted over 50 times in the past 400 years.
